text.p: Brazil coach Mario Zagallo said Thursday that he was not worried about facing Bolivia in La Paz at 3,600 metres above sea level in Sunday's Copa America.
"Our opponents on Sunday will be Bolivia, not the altitude," he said after Thursday's 7-0 semi-final demolition of Peru. "The altitude is there, it always has been."
He went on to refer to his own playing days as an example.

"In 1964, I went there with Botafogo. I played 90 minutes, you notice a bit of a difference but you can play perfectly well," he said. "We know from the start that if we reached the final and the final was against Bolivia, we would have to go there. I'm not here to complain."
Brazil have bad memories of Bolivia's largest city.
On their last visit four years ago, they suffered their first and only ever defeat in a World Cup qualifying match when they were beaten 2-0.

Zagallo said Brazil, who have played all their matches so far at near sea level in the country's second largest city of Santa Cruz, said they would arrive in La Paz only a couple of hours before the game in an attempt to minimise the altitude effects.
"We will have a light lunch around one o'clock and then we will fly to La Paz," he said. The game kicks off at six o'clock in the evening local time.

Zagallo, whose team has scored 18 goals and conceeded two in winning their five games so far, said he was delighted with the evolution of his team during the tournament, saying they were now playing the way he considered ideal.
"We have scored more goals than anyone else in the competition and our defence has conceded fewer than anyone else."
"In our first two games, we let our opponents create a lot of chances," he added. "Now, I think we are reaching our objective, not just for this competition but also for the World Cup next year."

Zagallo admitted that his star striker Ronaldo had been in the wrong when he was booked in the first half after lashing out at a rival. Ronaldo, who failed to score and missed an open goal in the second half, was substituted.
"He was being kicked by the Peruvian defence but he should never have got involved. He can't lose his head like that," Zagallo said.
